   211→            id: "payments",
   212→            title: "Payment integration",
   213→            filePath: ".local/tasks/payments.md",
   214→            dependsOn: ["auth"],
   215→        },
   216→    ]
   217→});

   220→## Plan File Format
   221→
   222→Write each project-task plan as a plain markdown document in `.local/tasks/`. The file content becomes the task description. Do not run `mkdir`; the write tool creates parent dirs.
   223→
   224→By default, create one project task per user request. Combine related work into a single plan rather than splitting into many tasks. Only create multiple tasks if the user explicitly asks for them or the request contains clearly independent, unrelated goals.
   225→
   226→Dependencies and artifact tags are not declared in the plan file — pass them via `dependsOn` and `artifactKinds` when creating or updating tasks.
   227→
   228→### Plan body
   229→
   230→First line: a short, descriptive title (3-6 words) prefixed with `#`. Then include these sections:
   231→
   232→- **What & Why** — Brief description of the feature/change and its purpose.
   233→- **Done looks like** — Observable outcomes when complete (what the user sees, not code-level details).
   234→- **Out of scope** — What is explicitly NOT included.
   235→- **Steps** — Numbered implementation steps for the executor agent, not separate project tasks.
   236→- **Relevant files** — Existing files discovered during investigation that the executor should start from. Use backtick-wrapped paths only, no trailing descriptions. Only list files you verified exist.
   237→  - Whole file: `src/api/billing.ts`
   238→  - Specific lines: `src/api/billing.ts:12-85`
   239→  - Multiple ranges: `src/api/billing.ts:12-85,200-250`
   240→  - WRONG: `src/api/billing.ts` — Billing API handlers (lines 12-85)
   241→

You may depend on existing tasks that are PENDING or later — never on existing PROPOSED tasks. Tasks within the same batch may depend on each other freely.
   243→

   245→
   246→- Each step should be describable in 1-2 sentences.
   247→- Focus on what to build, not how to build it.
   248→- Do not include file paths, code snippets, CSS classes, or line-level edits in step bullets. Put file references in `## Relevant files` instead.
   249→- Draw clean boundaries so parallel executors won't conflict. Combine same-area steps into one project task.
   250→- Add a short note for critical architectural constraints.
   251→
   252→### Example
   253→
   254→```markdown

   256→
   257→## What & Why
   258→Add Stripe payment processing so users can upgrade to paid plans.
   259→
   260→## Done looks like
   261→- Users can enter payment info and subscribe to a plan
   262→- Successful payments activate the paid tier immediately
   263→- Failed payments show a clear error message
   264→
   265→## Out of scope
   266→- Invoicing and receipts (future work)
   267→- Multiple payment methods (Stripe only for now)
   268→
   269→## Steps
   270→1. **Stripe backend integration** — Set up Stripe SDK, create endpoints for creating checkout sessions and handling webhooks
   271→2. **Payment UI** — Build the checkout page with plan selection and Stripe Elements for card input
   272→3. **Tier activation** — On successful payment, upgrade the user's account to the paid tier and reflect it in the UI
   273→
   274→## Relevant files
   275→- `src/api/billing.ts:12-85`
   276→- `src/config/stripe.ts`
   277→```

   279→### proposeProjectTasks(taskRefs)
   280→
   281→Propose existing tasks for user review. Pauses the agent until the user approves.
   282→
   283→**Parameters:**
   284→
   285→| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
   286→|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
   287→| `taskRefs` | array of str | Yes | Task refs to propose |
   288→

   290→
   291→**Example:**
   292→
   293→```javascript
   294→await proposeProjectTasks({ taskRefs: created.map(t => t.taskRef) });
   295→```
   296→
   297→## Task States
   298→
   299→| State | Description |
   300→|-------|-------------|
   301→| `PROPOSED` | Suggested but not yet accepted by the user. No implementation exists. |
   302→| `PENDING` | Accepted, waiting to start. No implementation exists. |
   303→| `IN_PROGRESS` | Being worked on by a task agent in a separate Repl. Changes are not visible in this Repl. |
   304→| `IMPLEMENTED` | Work is done in a separate Repl, ready for merge. Changes are not visible in this Repl — do not search the codebase for them. |
   305→| `MERGING` | Currently being merged. Do not duplicate. |
   306→| `MERGED` | Finished and merged. Changes are now visible in this Repl. |
   307→| `BLOCKED_BY_DRIFT` | Blocked because an upstream task diverged from its plan; needs replanning. |
   308→| `CANCELLED` | Abandoned. |
   309→
   310→## User Communication Rules
   311→
   312→Follow these rules strictly when discussing tasks with the user:
   313→
   314→1. **Always describe tasks by ref and title**: e.g. "Task #1 (Add authentication button)"
   315→2. **Never use internal state names**: use these display names instead:
   316→   - PROPOSED → "Drafts"
   317→   - PENDING → "Active"
   318→   - IN_PROGRESS → "Active"
   319→   - IMPLEMENTED → "Ready"
   320→   - MERGING → "Merging"
   321→   - MERGED → "Merged"
   322→   - CANCELLED → "Archived"
   323→   - BLOCKED_BY_DRIFT → "Affected by another task that changed"
   324→3. **Never expose implementation details**: Do not reveal function names (`bulkCreateProjectTasks`, `updateProjectTask`, etc.), API surface, or internal task system mechanics to the user
   325→
   326→## Best Practices
   327→
   328→1. **Prefer fewer tasks**: Default to one task per request unless the user explicitly asks for more
   329→2. **Create tasks early**: Create the project task when you understand the user's goals
   330→3. **Keep titles short**: Titles should be concise and descriptive
   331→4. **Use descriptions for detail**: Put implementation details in the description field
   332→
   333→## Example Workflow
   334→
   335→```javascript
   336→// 1. Write the plan file directly with the write tool — it creates `.local/tasks/` for you.
   337→
   338→// 2. Create the task — file content becomes the description
   339→const created = await bulkCreateProjectTasks({
   340→    tasks: [
   341→        {
   342→            title: "Launch microsite",
   343→            filePath: ".local/tasks/launch-microsite.md",
   344→            artifactKinds: ["web"],
   345→        },
   346→    ]
   347→});
   348→
   349→// 3. Propose for user approval (pauses agent loop)
   350→await proposeProjectTasks({
   351→    taskRefs: created.map(t => t.taskRef),
   352→});
   353→
   354→// --- After user approves, the system handles scheduling ---
   355→
   356→// 4. Check progress
   357→const tasks = await listProjectTasks();
   358→for (const task of tasks) {
   359→    console.log(`Task ${task.taskRef} (${task.title}): ${task.state}`);
   360→}

# Integrations Skill

Integrations allow first-class usage of Third-Party (and some First-party) technologies. If the integration exists, you can ask user to "connect" their account (Google, Linear, GitHub, Stripe, etc) to their Replit account, which critically gives you, the Replit Agent, access to new capabilities (e.g. view their Google Sheets, read their Linear issues, setup & access payment systems, etc). You must follow the  steps outlined here to successfully make these "connections".

**Before asking the user for any API key, secret, or credential, always search for a Replit integration first.** Replit integrations handle OAuth and secrets securely, and many common services (Google Sheets, Linear, Stripe, GitHub, OpenAI, etc.) are already supported. Asking the user for credentials when an integration exists adds a lot of unnecessary friction. Users typically do not know about our integration system, you must proactive in suggesting it when it (and only when) it is relevant.

Integrations include blueprints (code templates), connectors (OAuth/API integrations + templates), and connections (already established integrations).

## When to Use

Use this skill when:

- User needs authentication (login, signup, OAuth)
- User needs database connections (PostgreSQL, MongoDB, etc.)
- User needs payment processing (Stripe, etc.)
- User needs third-party API integrations (OpenAI, Notion, GitHub, Linear, etc.)
- User asks about Replit-specific features and capabilities

## When NOT to Use

As a web search (use web-search skill if available), searching files within the project, media generation (use media-generation skill, including image generation APIs), fetching data to respond to a user's question (use query-integration-data skill).

---

## Integration Lifecycle

There are three types of integrations, and they represent different stages of a lifecycle:

```text
connector (not_setup)
    → user completes OAuth via proposeIntegration
    → connection (not_added)
        → addIntegration        ← code-side wiring (npm packages, scaffolds, project registration)
        → proposeIntegration    ← platform-side binding (registers this Repl with connectors so the credential proxy will serve secrets)
        → now it is a functioning connection (added + authorized, ready to use)

blueprint (not_installed)
    → addIntegration or proposeIntegration
    → blueprint (installed, code + packages added to project), ready to use
```

### Connectors

- An available OAuth/API integration that has **not yet been authorized** by the user
- Status: `not_setup`
- Cannot be added directly — must use `proposeIntegration` which allows the user through the OAuth flow
- Example ID: `connector:ccfg_google-sheet_E42A9F6DA6...`

### Connections

- A connector that has **already been authorized** at the account level
- Status: `not_added` (authorized at account level but not bound to this Repl) or `added` (active in this Repl)
- Both `addIntegration` AND `proposeIntegration` are required on first setup — they do orthogonal things:
  - `addIntegration` does code-side wiring (npm install, scaffolds, project registration). It does NOT touch the platform's connection-state backend.
  - `proposeIntegration` does platform-side binding (registers this Repl with connectors-v2 as a permitted consumer). Without it the credential proxy at `connectors.replit.com/api/v2/connection` returns nothing for this Repl, even though the underlying credentials exist at the account level.
- Example ID: `connection:conn_linear_01MG99PAJR6MQ5...`

NOTE: You must not delay calling proposeIntegration even if it waits for the user. You will be blocked and not have access to test the feature you build because you don't have access to real data, real APIs, etc, which is even more inefficient than reaching out to the user as soon as you know you need the integration to get accepted.

### Blueprints

- These are just code templates that install packages and scaffold integration boilerplate
- Status: `not_installed` or `previously_installed`
- Use `addIntegration` directly; if `requiresConfirmation` is True, use `proposeIntegration` instead
- Example ID: `blueprint:javascript_openai`

### searchIntegrations(query)

Search for available integrations. **Always run this first.** Try a few different query terms if the first search returns nothing — results depend on keyword matching.

arguments.description: Find content stream assembly in contour PDF export

content.text:
No — the CutContour is **not grouped with the image**. They share the same PDF page but are kept as separate, independent content streams.

Here's how it's assembled in `downloadContourPDF`:

- The image is drawn into the page's original content stream.
- The CutContour path is built separately (`combinedPathOps`), registered as its **own** content stream, and then **appended to the page's `Contents` array** (lines 2595–2607: `context.stream(...)` → `context.register(...)` → `existingContents.push(contentStreamRef)`).

So the page ends up with an array of content streams. PDF renders them sequentially as one logical stream — image first, then the cut line stroked on top — but there is **no grouping construct** tying them together:

- No Form XObject wrapping the image + cut path into a single object
- No marked-content sequence (`BDC`/`EMC`)
- No Optional Content Group / layer (no `/OCG`, no `/OC`)

Each path block is wrapped only in its own `q` … `Q` (graphics-state save/restore), which isolates graphics state — it does not "group" the objects.

How the cutter actually finds the cut line: it's painted in a **Separation color space named after the label** (CutContour / PerfCutContour / KissCut — see the `Separation` / `DeviceCMYK` setup at lines 2622–2637 for the locked contour, same pattern for the active one). RIPs and cutters identify the cut path by that **spot-color name**, not by any grouping. So grouping with the image is neither needed nor desirable — keeping it as its own separation stroke is exactly what print/cut workflows expect.

The same applies to a second (locked) contour and to the white/gloss spot-color fills: each is its own appended content stream with its own separation color space, none of them grouped with the image.
